decisions: The owner session is a four-hour signed Secure HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie, with login failures handled by a bounded in-memory rate limiter.
Supabase product reads stay server-only: the server credential is used as apikey and only JWT-shaped credentials may also be sent as bearer authorization.
The repeatable persistence verifier is the minimal Docker-local Supabase stack with migrations and no seeded product data.
The acceptance browser path uses the real Fastify session and live local Supabase; route interception is limited to isolated UI-state tests.
Generated local Supabase branches and temporary runtime state are ignored and excluded from the container context.
deviations_from_plan: Local verification used an empty temporary Docker credential configuration and a minimal Supabase service set because the Docker Desktop credential helper stalled and optional image pulls were rate-limited; product scope and acceptance criteria were unchanged.
Two staff-review correction cycles were required to align authentication, live-read, responsive-state, and secret-boundary behavior; no acceptance criterion was weakened.

commits: 76985ff feat(S01-02): add durable Telegram ingress seam

decisions: The webhook secret is timing-safe compared in Fastify onRequest before body parsing or any repository, owner-state, or Telegram call.
Only the configured numeric owner in the matching private chat is accepted; every unauthorized or non-private update receives the same generic Telegram refusal and an opaque HTTP acknowledgement.

A security-definer Postgres function atomically claims the unique update identity and captures the optional authenticated owner delivery chat; the persistence interface accepts no webhook payload or message text.
The controlled walking-skeleton responses are exactly 'No active promises.' for empty status and one bounded status-guidance line for other owner text; model and commitment behavior remain deferred.
A claimed update is never processed or sent twice, including concurrent replay; outbound Telegram is isolated behind an injectable server-only client.
deviations_from_plan: The QA sandbox denied approved disposable-database mutation and local Playwright port binding, so the lead context executed the immutable Node 24 commands while QA independently reproduced the webhook test and reviewed the results, migration, tests, state, and redaction scans; evidence records this split provenance.

One self-cleaning test attempt was abandoned and fully restored because cleanup would have required broadening intentionally narrow production table permissions; the disposable local database was reset from committed migrations after QA instead.
follow_ups: S01-03: replace the temporary unsupported-text guidance path with the bounded decision and draft flow while preserving the Telegram authorization, claim, and redaction seams.
S01-06: extend /status from the factual empty response to ordered active promises with versioned Done and Cancel actions.
S01-12: configure the deployed Telegram webhook and record a real owner/private, unauthorized, and replay-safe smoke without exposing identifiers or message text.
log.context_for_next:
Telegram ingress is stable at POST /api/telegram/webhook with secret validation before JSON parsing.
TelegramService owns owner/private-chat checks and uses injected client and repository seams.
The exact generic refusal and empty-status responses are frozen; HTTP acknowledgements remain opaque.
Postgres atomically claims unique update IDs and captures the single owner delivery chat without retaining payloads or message text.
Concurrent replay produces one claim, send, and completion; later deliveries do nothing.
The local database has been reset from both committed migrations and contains no synthetic QA rows.
All exact S01-02 commands and the full Node 24 gate pass; evidence records the QA execution bridge.
S01-03 and S01-07 are dependency-eligible; preserve the Telegram security and minimization boundary.
